Welcome to Music
Curriculum Intent
The Music curriculum at Evelyn Grace Academy aims to develop a deep appreciation of music by harnessing students’ performance, composing and listening skills. Students will explore a number of instrumental disciplines and topics to ensure they adopt a valuable musical skills set that transcends well beyond the music classroom. Music study, in conjunction with other subjects, provides a broad, rounded education to equips students with all the necessary tools to go on and be successful irrespective of their chosen path following secondary education. Participation in music encourages and nurtures a number of attributes including; confidence, wellbeing, discipline, social cohesion, communication skills and teamwork. It also provides a strong platform for students to make a positive contribution to the wider school community. To facilitate the development of these skills the Music Department provides the following opportunities for students at the academy. Instrumental Lessons: Students can study a variety of instruments at Evelyn Grace Academy. We recognise the importance instrumental study plays in a child’s cognitive development and wellbeing so lessons are provided to students totally free. Students can study piano, steel pans, drums, bass guitar, guitar (acoustic/electronic), violin, voice and trumpet.
Head of Department
Mr Jacob Blair

Welcome to PHSE and Citizenship
Curriculum Intent
The CPSHE curriculum prepares our students to be the voice of their future. The purpose of this curriculum is to prepare all of our students with the skills and knowledge needed over and above that contained within our academic curriculum so that they can thrive as they journey through life; at school and beyond. We believe that one of the most important elements of a young person’s education is the opportunities provided which help them to develop personally, these are essential if we are going to ensure that our students are happy and able to achieve success in a challenging, complex and changing world. Our ever-evolving and reflective Personal Development curriculum seeks to support and guide students to navigate and develop all aspects of their character, whilst being respectful of others. Our programme is underpinned by our five school values; Community, Professionalism, Integrity, Ambition and Perseverance; and through our programme, students learn how to understand these values, debate them and demonstrate them in everything that they do. This in itself, supports students' appreciation of British values – their spiritual moral social and cultural development Our programme exposes students to many of the great people that have shaped the world we live in; the best that has been thought and the best that has been said. These people hail from a wide range backgrounds, and at all times the programme seeks to promote diversity and advocate respect for protected characteristics. It provides our students with opportunities to flourish as leaders and offers a wide range of opportunities inside and outside of the school that spark passion, interest and a thirst for life and learning. It allows space for healthy discussion and debate as well as providing support, guidance and learning around wellbeing, relationships and safety. Our programme aims to ensure that every student at Evelyn Grace Academy School develops independent characters - someone that is the best, most authentic version of themselves. We hope that, through this process, students can obtain the cultural capital that will allow them to build a happy, fulfilled and successful life for themselves beyond Evelyn Grace Academy School.
Head of Department
Mr Max Deckers-Dowber

This includes tutor time, assemblies, drop down days and the work we do with external partners such as Brook. We run a full democratic school council programme which all students are involved in teaching them the values of fairness, justice, respect, rule of law and democracy.

Welcome to Business Studies
Curriculum Intent
The intent of the Business Studies curriculum at Ark Evelyn Grace Academy is to spark pupils’ imagination and inspire commercial thinking for the wider world as they develop their business knowledge and acumen. The contemporary business context of this course, marries the theory and practical aspect of business and enterprise to engage students inside and outside the classroom. The department seeks to enable strong performances in both comprehension and analytical skills through the examination of case studies and current affairs with the aim of molding astute and aware young adults who can be the voice of their future.
Ms Rachael Fernandes

Welcome to Design and Technology
Curriculum Intent
At Ark Evelyn Grace Academy we aim to inspire students to design, make, evaluate and test products to solve real world problems that occur in our daily lives. Design and Technlogy brings together a number of different disciplines and is therefore taught across a range of subjects. Across these multiple disciplinary areas in lessons and specialist sessions students will develp technical skills and nutrional knowledge and plan, investigate, develop and evaluate ideas so that they are well equipped to be the voice of their future.

Our careers programme
Mission Statement
"Every student will find an individual pathway to University and Career Success based on informed decisions and in-depth Careers Education Information and Guidance (CEIAG)"
At Ark Evelyn Grace Academy we use the gold standard Gatsby Benchmarks: a nationally-recognised framework used to define and develop a first-class careers provision. The framework consists of the following elements:
A stable careers programme
Learning from career and labour market information
Addressing the needs of each pupil
Linking curriculum learning to careers
Encounters with employers and employees
Experiences of workplaces
Encounters with further and higher education
Personal guidance
Our Careers Lead
Mr Max Deckers-Dowber

Performing arts
In addition to instrumental lessons, the Music Department also facilitates a number of clubs which are free to join. Below is an outline of the current provision: ● Mondays – Bossa Nova Club – During lunchtime ● Tuesdays - Bands - During lunchtime ● Wednesday – Choir – Lunchtime and after school ● Wednesdays - Music Technology Club - After school ● Thursdays – Brass – During lunchtime ● Fridays – Strings – During lunchtime The music department is also open every break and lunchtime for students to practice in any of the band or practice rooms.
Ark Music Network: Within the Ark Network there are extensive opportunities for students to further develop their musicianship by participating in a variety of external ensemble groups within the trust. These include: ● Spark – Choir ● Chamber Choir ● Fusion – Instrumental Ensemble ● Rap Collective Concerts & Performance Opportunities: There are also a number of performance opportunities for students to participate in throughout the academic year. ● Open Mic – Monthly performances in the lunch hall ● Winter Music Concert ● Spring Music Concert ● Summer Music Concert ● KS3 Celebration of Achievement ● KS4 Celebration of Achievement ● School Productions ● Assemblies Workshops, Trips & Outreach The Music Department has facilitated a number of trips, workshops and outreach projects including: ● Music Master
Classes ● ELAM Music GCSE Workshops ● Songwriting workshops at the Roundhouse ● Gamelan Workshops at the Royal Festival Hall ● Concerts at the Barbican – Ark Gala
